newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to discuss cabinet changes with Russian PM.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to discuss cabinet changes with Russian PM.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin was due to meet Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Tuesday to discuss a cabinet reshuffle and plans for a summit with U.S. President Bill Clinton, Interfax news agency said.
Interfax quoted presidential press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky as saying the government shake-up, expected to be announced later this week, would be less radical than some media have predicted.
It will not be "as global as some mass media write", Yastrzhembsky said, but gave no details. Chernomyrdin promised last week the cabinet changes would be more than cosmetic.

Itar-Tass news agency said the regular weekly meeting between Yeltsin and Chernomyrdin would start at midday (0900 GMT) and they would also discuss a keynote speech which the president is to make to parliament on Thursday.
Yeltsin criticised the government's failure to pay wages on time during talks with Chernomyrdin last week and the prime minister promised to make proposals for a cabinet reshuffle.

Some newspapers have suggested Chernomyrdin could be fired, but others have ruled out his dismissal, concentrating their speculation on the fate of ministers dealing with the economy and social policy.
Defence Minister Igor Rodionov's future is also in question after Yeltsin criticised him publicly last week.
Yastrzhembsky said Yeltsin and Chernomyrdin would discuss the Russia-U.S. summit planned for Helsinki on March 20-21 but gave no details.
Other topics would include progress in paying pensions and wages and the overall economic and financial situation, he said.
